title: Philippians Bible Quiz - Chapter 3
description: Ten questions on Philippians 3: no confidence in the flesh, counting all things loss for Christ, and pressing on toward the goal.

questions.text: Of what three things does verse 2 tell them to beware?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says "Beware of the dogs; beware of the evil workers; beware of the false circumcision."

answers.text: The rulers, the scribes, and the soldiers
The dogs, the evil workers, and the false circumcision
The idle, the drunken, and the greedy
The rich, the proud, and the mockers

questions.text: Of which tribe does the writer say he is?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says he was circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews.

answers.text: The tribe of Judah
The tribe of Levi
The tribe of Ephraim
The tribe of Benjamin

questions.text: Concerning the law, what does he say he was?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says that concerning the law, he was a Pharisee.

answers.text: A Pharisee
A scribe
A Sadducee
A priest

questions.text: What does he say he counts all things to be, for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says he counts all things to be a loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus, and counts them nothing but refuse.

answers.text: A shadow of better things
A debt still to be paid
A loss, nothing but refuse
A gain he may yet keep

questions.text: What kind of righteousness does he want to be found with?
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says he wants to be found in him, not having a righteousness of his own from the law, but the righteousness which is through faith in Christ, from God by faith.

answers.text: The righteousness which is his own, from the law
The righteousness of the fathers before the law
The righteousness that is measured by zeal
The righteousness which is from God by faith in Christ

questions.text: What does verse 10 say he desires to know?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says he desires to know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, becoming conformed to his death.

answers.text: Him, the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings
The times and the seasons which the Father has set
The mystery hidden from all the generations before him
The secrets of the law and of the prophets of old

questions.text: What does he say in verse 12 about having already obtained or been made perfect?
questions.explanation: Verse 12 says he has not already obtained, nor is he already made perfect, but he presses on to take hold of that for which he was taken hold of by Christ Jesus.

answers.text: He has, and now teaches others
He does not say, because no one can know
He has not, but he presses on
He has obtained, but is not yet made perfect

questions.text: What is the "one thing" he says he does?
questions.explanation: Verse 13 says that, not regarding himself as having taken hold, he does one thing: forgetting the things which are behind, and stretching forward to the things which are before.

answers.text: Praying without ceasing for all of the assemblies
Forgetting what is behind and stretching forward to what is before
Keeping the rule he received from the fathers
Boasting only in his own weakness and sufferings

questions.text: What does verse 19 say about those he calls enemies of the cross of Christ?
questions.explanation: Verse 19 says their end is destruction, their god is the belly, their glory is in their shame, and they think about earthly things.

answers.text: They will be restored at the last day
They were once teachers in the assembly
They keep the law but deny the Spirit
Their end is destruction and their god is the belly

questions.text: Where does verse 20 say our citizenship is?
questions.explanation: Verse 20 says our citizenship is in heaven, from where we also wait for a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ.

answers.text: In heaven
In Jerusalem
In Philippi
In Macedonia
